paper_type_rationale: VAGNet proposes a new task (video-guided 3D affordance grounding), a new architecture (MCAM + STFM), a new dataset (PVAD), and a new state-of-the-art on it. The dominant contribution is a method/dataset paper with AI-method character.
must_cover: New task definition: video-guided 3D affordance grounding
PVAD dataset construction and Seen/Unseen protocols
Main quantitative results vs. XMF/IAGNet/GREAT/PointTalk-Baseline on PVAD
Ablation isolating MCAM, STFM, and the full 2D branch
key_numbers: PVAD: 3,763 videos; 36,765 point clouds; 38 categories; 22 affordance types; max 10s per clip
Seen aIoU: VAGNet 42.96 vs GREAT 40.23 (+2.73); VAGNet-img 41.58
Ablation w/o 2D branch & MCAM: Unseen aIoU 11.64; w/o STFM: 10.25; w/o MCAM: 11.98; Full: 12.09
Training: 60 epochs, batch 12, 1x RTX 4090, AdamW, lr 1e-4, wd 1e-6, cosine schedule
Video: 8 uniformly-sampled frames; TimeSformer frozen, Kinetics-600 pretrained
real_comparisons: VAGNet vs. GREAT (static SOTA): consistent gains on Seen and Unseen; largest on Unseen aIoU/MAE
VAGNet vs. VAGNet-img: video input adds further gains on top of architectural contribution
VAGNet vs. Baseline (PointTalk-adapted video-3D): VAGNet wins by a large margin, showing affordance-specific fusion matters
VAGNet vs. XMF (completion repurposed): VAGNet wins; repurposed completion is insufficient for affordance

central_claims.claim: Using HOI videos as the primary functional supervision yields more accurate 3D affordance grounding than static (image/text) cues.
supporting_evidence: Sec.4.2 Table 1: VAGNet > all static baselines on Seen/Unseen aIoU/AUC/SIM/MAE
Sec.4.3 Table 2: removing video-conditioned modules degrades all metrics
Sec.4.4 Fig.4 qualitative: VAGNet covers full functional regions where single-image methods miss parts
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: Within the PVAD protocol and the compared baselines, video-guided grounding outperforms static-cue grounding.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not prove this gap generalizes to all open-vocabulary settings, partial observations, or robots in the wild; PVAD assumes aligned video-point-cloud pairs and 38/22 category coverage.

central_claims.claim: The MCAM + STFM two-stage design is necessary; neither module alone reproduces the full performance.
supporting_evidence: Sec.4.3 Table 2: w/o MCAM loses Unseen generalization (aIoU 11.98 vs 12.09); w/o STFM loses Unseen more (aIoU 10.25); w/o both loses the most
Sec.4.3 Fig.5: contextual attention maps progressively highlight affordance regions as MCAM integrates video frames
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: Within the four-variant ablation, the two modules contribute complementary evidence for Seen vs Unseen.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not prove this exact split is optimal; alternative fusions or joint training strategies are not exhaustively compared.

central_claims.claim: An affordance-aware 2D projection + cross-attention is an effective interface for injecting 2D context into 3D features.
supporting_evidence: Sec.3.3 Eq.(1)-(4) and the architecture's cross-attention injection
VAGNet-img (no video) still beats GREAT, showing the 2D-projection-based injection has standalone value
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: It proves the injection design works on PVAD; it does not prove the specific view-planning or 3x3 patch size is optimal.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: Robustness to bad view planning, extreme occlusion, or sparse-view inputs is not evaluated.

central_claims.claim: PVAD is a useful benchmark for video-grounded affordance.
supporting_evidence: Sec.3.2: 3,763 videos, 36,765 point clouds, 38 categories, 22 affordance types with Seen/Unseen splits
All baselines perform worse than VAGNet, showing the benchmark is non-trivial
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: PVAD is large enough to separate methods; it does not prove the categories/exemplars are representative of all real HOIs.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: Whether PVAD covers long-tail affordances or noisy in-the-wild videos; whether the 10s clip cap limits temporal modeling.

claim_boundaries: VAGNet is not zero-video at inference: the claim is 'zero heavy model' (no LLM teacher), not 'zero video input'.
PVAD assumes point clouds are complete; partial-observation robustness is not studied.
Unseen split aIoU is still around 12 across all methods, leaving a large generalization gap.
The ablation uses 4 variants; finer-grained ablations (e.g., patch size, frame count, view-planning strategy) are not reported.
negative_or_limiting_results: Baseline (PointTalk video-3D) underperforms even XMF, indicating naive video-3D fusion is not enough.
Unseen aIoU for all methods is around 12 (vs ~40 on Seen), showing large generalization gap.
No frame-count sensitivity: only 8 frames reported.
VAGNet-img (image only) is still close to GREAT but loses to full VAGNet, isolating the video contribution.
mechanism_result_map: 2D contextual attention (Eq.1-2) -> MCAM aligns projection with video frames -> enables cross-attention injection to anchor evidence on the 3D surface (Table 2 w/o MCAM drops Unseen aIoU).
Spatial-temporal cross-attention in STFM (Eq.5-6) -> fuses time-evolving contact cues with 3D geometry -> drives the Unseen generalization (Table 2 w/o STFM drops Unseen aIoU to 10.25).
Focal+Dice loss on per-point heatmap -> handles class imbalance and region overlap -> stable optimization under sparse affordance labels.
Affordance-aware view planning -> ensures the projection contains interaction-rich viewpoints -> supplies MCAM with meaningful foreground/background pairs.
comparative_positioning: Vs. IAGNet/GREAT (image-3D): VAGNet adds video, giving dynamic functional supervision that static images cannot.
Vs. PointTalk/Ego-SAG (video-point cloud): VAGNet focuses on object-level affordance rather than scene-level, and is lighter than Ego-SAG's learnable bilateral queries.
Vs. Affostruction (completion-based): orthogonal; Affostruction assumes complete shape while VAGNet uses video as functional prior (not completion).
Vs. HAMMER (MLLM intent, single-image): VAGNet does not use MLLM; it uses frozen TimeSformer. The two are complementary in spirit (dynamic vs language intent).
reuse_takeaways: Affordance-aware 2D projection + MCAM-style 2D-to-3D cross-attention is a reusable template for grounding 2D evidence on 3D surfaces.
STFM's time-axis cross-attention is a clean way to inject temporal context into 3D features without a heavy temporal backbone.
Building a video-grounded affordance benchmark requires careful video-clip trimming and a Seen/Unseen protocol to expose generalization gaps.
followup_questions: Can the MCAM injection be distilled into a video-free 3D branch (true zero-video grounding)?
What is the minimum video length / frame count needed to retain VAGNet's gain?
Does VAGNet still work when the point cloud is partial / incomplete (closer to real robot input)?
Can the dynamic supervision be replaced by an MLLM-derived intent signal, and how do the two compare?
How sensitive is the model to view-planning errors and to extreme occlusions?

section_plan.focus: Restate the static-cue failure modes and motivate video-guided grounding.
section_plan.reading_goal: Make the reader feel that affordance is action-defined, not geometry-defined.

section_plan.focus: Define the task, the PVAD splits, and the four evaluation metrics.
section_plan.reading_goal: Let the reader judge what VAGNet is and is not being evaluated on.

section_plan.focus: Walk through MCAM, STFM, the loss, and the projection choices with key equations.
section_plan.reading_goal: Make the architecture and training objective reproducible at the level of a senior graduate student.

section_plan.focus: Present the main table, the ablation, and the qualitative analysis side by side.
section_plan.reading_goal: Let the reader see which numbers come from which design choice.

section_plan.focus: Explain why MCAM+STFM works, discuss cost and extensibility, and flag reproduction gotchas.
section_plan.reading_goal: Turn the paper into actionable guidance for the reader's own project.

section_plan.focus: Catalog honest limitations: video dependence, Unseen gap, frame-count fixity, no failure-case analysis.
section_plan.reading_goal: Prevent the reader from over-claiming what the paper proves.
